<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <Description>
      The official .NET library for performing CRUD opertations on Agents in Microsoft Foundry.

      This library features the client to perform Agent administration operations. It depends on and builds from the official OpenAI library for .NET to maintain rapid upstream feature propagation and
      ongoing forward compatibility.
    </Description>
    <AssemblyTitle>Microsoft Azure.AI.Projects.Agents client library</AssemblyTitle>
    <Version>3.0.0-beta.6</Version>
    <!--The ApiCompatVersion is managed automatically and should not generally be modified manually.-->
    <ApiCompatVersion>2.0.0</ApiCompatVersion>
    <PackageTags>Azure.AI.Projects.Agents</PackageTags>
    <TargetFrameworks>$(RequiredTargetFrameworks)</TargetFrameworks>
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <IncludeOperationsSharedSource>true</IncludeOperationsSharedSource>
    <IncludeSystemClientModelSharedSourceForTracing>true</IncludeSystemClientModelSharedSourceForTracing>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="OpenAI" />
    <PackageReference Include="Azure.Core" />
    <PackageReference Include="Azure.AI.Extensions.OpenAI" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <Compile Include="$(AzureCoreSharedSources)ExperimentalAttribute.cs" LinkBase="Shared" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>

proposals.subtype: Instrument binary agent-creation protocol calls
proposals.explanation: The sync/async BinaryContent CreateAgent methods start a create-agent scope, validate content, process a created pipeline message and record the response with BufferResponse. Their try catches Exception, records it on the optional scope and rethrows; scope startup and input validation occur before that try.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten-marker partial under src/Custom implements these protocol methods outside Generated with explicit OpenTelemetryScope calls.

proposals.subtype: Instrument binary agent-version creation with response/error hooks
proposals.explanation: The BinaryContent CreateAgentVersion pair starts a version-creation scope, validates name/content, processes a request carrying foundryFeatures, records the response and rethrows exceptions after RecordError inside the try. The async processing uses ConfigureAwait(false); scope helper internals are not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten src/Custom REST partial contains executable telemetry hooks around both protocol calls.

proposals.subtype: Instrument manifest-based version protocol calls as version creation
proposals.explanation: The BinaryContent CreateAgentVersionFromManifest pair uses StartCreateAgentVersion, validates name/content, invokes its manifest request factory and records version-creation responses or caught exceptions before returning/rethrowing. Validation remains outside the catch, and the actual manifest payload/request factory is absent.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten REST partial under src/Custom explicitly implements these manifest protocol telemetry wrappers.

proposals.subtype: Instrument manifest agent creation using create-agent telemetry
proposals.explanation: The BinaryContent CreateAgentFromManifest pair starts a create-agent scope, validates content, processes the manifest request and records create-agent responses. Exceptions inside its try are recorded then rethrown. EditorBrowsable(Never) affects discovery, not public accessibility.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten src/Custom REST partial supplies these concrete manifest protocol method bodies.

proposals.subtype: Instrument binary agent-update protocol calls
proposals.explanation: The BinaryContent UpdateAgent pair starts an update scope, validates name/content, passes foundryFeatures to its request factory, processes the request and records the response. It records/rethrows exceptions inside its try. Adding a version only when changed is documented service behavior, not a local comparison algorithm in these methods.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten REST partial under src/Custom contains explicit update response/error instrumentation.

proposals.subtype: Adapt cancellation and typed results for version lookup
proposals.explanation: The CancellationToken GetAgentVersion pair calls AssertNotNullOrEmpty for both identifiers, delegates to the RequestOptions overload using ToRequestOptions and converts through ToProjectAgentsResult<ProjectsAgentVersion>. The async call awaits with ConfigureAwait(false); the conversion helper's implementation is absent.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten src/Custom REST partial adds these complete typed overloads outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Construct distinct token-provider and options-only pipelines
proposals.explanation: The token-provider constructor validates endpoint/provider, creates fixed ai.azure.com scope and common authorization-URL flow metadata, and inserts UserAgentPolicy, BearerTokenPolicy and a fixed FoundryFeaturesPolicy list. The options-only constructor explicitly inserts only UserAgentPolicy. Both default options, retain endpoint/version and construct diagnostics; their user-agent assembly arguments differ. Options may supply other behavior not shown here.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten-marker client partial under src/Custom implements both concrete pipeline constructors outside Generated.

proposals.handwrittenRationale: The handwritten src/Custom client partial adds the executable sync/async typed wrappers.

limitations: Only two of 785 eligible files were captured among 836 discovered files. The REST excerpt ends at 420 in UpdateAgentFromManifest documentation and the client excerpt at 309 in GetAgentVersions documentation; dozens of named budget skips include telemetry, collection adapters, request/serialization helpers, session/voice/toolbox code and generator stubs.

OpenTelemetryScope and its recording/privacy/enablement rules are absent. Findings establish hook placement, not actual emitted spans, tags, request contents or metrics. Scope startup and argument assertions precede the protocol try/catch, so that catch is not an all-error recording guarantee.

Generated requests/models, result converters, serializer context, policy implementations and custom collection adapters are not supplied. Their auth behavior, exact JSON, paging protocol and service semantics are not inferred from imports or comments.

Manifest-based typed creation validates manifestId without explicitly forwarding it in the shown body; its optional-null options signature also calls AssertNotNull, and the sync fallback initialization follows that assertion. These are literal source observations, not runtime-verified defects.

Suppression-only findings describe the exact visible generated member families without inventing replacement behavior. Suppressions paired with captured typed version/manifest creation and agent-list replacements are included with those findings rather than counted again.

Private cached-subclient fields, shared operation dependencies and uncaptured method documentation are not separate customizations. The findings do not establish package-wide coverage, an LRO, or an uncaptured session-log streaming implementation.

Review covers only two handwritten-marker excerpts (REST client lines 1-420 and client lines 1-309) from 785 eligible files; 783 eligible files, remaining lines of these two files, and skipped custom/helper sources are not assessed. Partial evidence cannot establish absence of other customizations.

Generated counterparts, request factories, typed-result conversion, collection-result pagination/deserialization, telemetry scope internals, pipeline-policy implementations and replacement methods named by suppression annotations are not supplied; these conclusions concern visible source only, not verified runtime behavior.

The client constructors also contain a fixed FoundryFeaturesPolicy and different user-agent policies; the version-creation convenience methods also serialize options. These distinct candidate behaviors use the same source-path-plus-symbol identity as existing findings, so the stable-key rule forbids separate omissions without duplicating an original/effective identity. The accepted/revised findings must not be read as exhaustive coverage of those symbols.

A CodeGenSuppress attribute establishes author intent to suppress the named generated signature, but without the generated output its prior existence and effective public accessibility cannot be independently confirmed. Accepted denotes AI review, not human or runtime verification.
